analysis: The only changed file is a test file, provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Engine/EngineV2BridgeTests.swift. Changes: StubTokenizer gains a decodeTable so chosen ids decode to custom text (head 146-147, 155); makeBridge gains a stopStringScope parameter passed through to EngineV2Bridge (head 443, 462); and three new tests were added (head 847-899). The tests exercise scoped stop-string matching (ReasoningStopScope, ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope), request-level scope reaching the CBv2 engine request, and request scope overriding the model scope. None of this ships in production binaries. No threat-model assets, trust boundaries, authorization, attestation, encryption, cache storage, or billing logic changes. The tests do reference behavior that production code presumably implements elsewhere: EngineV2Bridge.matchedStopSequence with a scope argument, submitTokenized(stopStringScope:), and the bridge init stopStringScope parameter. The production implementation is outside the supplied evidence, so I did not verify it. That behavior is a stop-string/reasoning-scope correctness feature rather than a security control. It touches A-001 only indirectly, through the output-truncation semantics of stop sequences, and creates no confidentiality exposure that is visible here. The patch excerpt is truncated, but the base and head ranges cover the full change. No regressions or new attack surface were identified in this unit. Integration should confirm that the production EngineV2Bridge/EngineV2Translation changes in other files of the PR do not alter cache-scope (cacheSalt) plumbing relevant to T-041.
